claims: Commander Reid Wiseman, Pilot Victor Glover, Mission Specialist Christina Koch (NASA), and Mission Specialist Jeremy Hansen (Canadian Space Agency).
Artemis II is set to fly a 10-day mission around the Moon.
Artemis II is scheduled to launch on April 1, 2026.
The Artemis II crew includes the first Black astronaut to travel to deep space.
The Artemis II crew includes the first Canadian to travel to deep space.
The Artemis II crew will pilot the Orion spacecraft titled Integrity.
Artemis II is a flight test of the SLS rocket.
Reid Wiseman is the Commander for Artemis II from NASA.
Reid Wiseman leads the Artemis II mission.
Reid Wiseman is responsible for the overall safety and success of the Artemis II crew.
Artemis II is a 10-day, approximately 600,000-mile journey.
Victor Glover is the Pilot for Artemis II from NASA.
Victor Glover is responsible for piloting the Orion spacecraft and verifying its systems.
Victor Glover serves as second in command for Artemis II.
Christina Koch is a Mission Specialist for Artemis II from NASA.
Christina Koch is the primary mission specialist supporting navigation, communications, and system operations during Artemis II.
Jeremy Hansen is a Mission Specialist for Artemis II from the Canadian Space Agency (CSA).
Jeremy Hansen is the Canadian Space Agency representative for Artemis II.
Jeremy Hansen contributes to critical tasks, technology tests, and scientific research.
The Artemis II crew will travel in the Orion spacecraft powered by the Space Launch System (SLS) rocket.
Artemis II is scheduled for launch from Kennedy Space Center, Florida.
The objective of Artemis II is to test all systems necessary for deep space human exploration.
The objective of Artemis II is to prepare for future lunar missions.
